title: Adaptive Funnel Scheduler for Multi-Phase Compute Paths (arch + seq-len aware)
creator: Michael Liu
description:
Problem: Our current single-pass kernel pickers sometimes choose suboptimal compute primitives for mixed prefill/decode workloads across heterogeneous hardware. This shows up as unexpected 95th percentile latency regressions on mid-sized sequence lengths (128-512) for some customer workloads when we favor throughput-optimized kernels. Goals: 1) Reduce tail latency regressions for mixed burst workloads (target 95p reduction >= 30% on affected profiles). 2) Maintain or improve token/sec for steady-state decode (<10% regression). 3) Provide fast online adaptation with low overhead (probe cost < 0.5% of tokens). Solution summary: Implement a \"funnel\"-style, multi-stage scheduler that (a) cheaply probes a small subset of candidate kernels per compute-path using microbenchmarks during warmstart, (b) feeds probe outcomes plus request features (arch, batch size, prefix length, avg seq len, KV cache hit flag) into a lightweight cost regressor to predict latency and throughput trade-offs, and (c) chooses a kernel profile with a staged fallback policy for safety.

Distinguishing points versus prior approaches:
- The funnel stages are explicitly split into: microprobe (fast single-token kernel microbench), sampled warmstart (short live inference on low-priority flow), and steady-state selection.
- Prefill vs decode phases are decoupled: probe signals for prefill consider memory layout and occupancy, while decode probes emphasize launch overhead and token generation steady-state.
- We integrate KV cache hit rate as a first-class feature; kernels that shine on cold-prefill but degrade with high cache reuse are penalized during decode-phase selection.
- Lightweight model: a small XGBoost-like regressor (serialized C++ model) that runs in the hot path but is optimized for vectorized feature evaluation; retrain cadence is weekly from aggregated microprobe telemetry.

Safety & rollout:
- Always keep a conservative fallback kernel (high compatibility, predictable latency).
- Canary rollout by customer tier: internal traffic (dev) -> canary tenants (small set) -> 10% production -> full.

Metrics and heuristics:
- Scoring function prioritizes 95p latency and 99p safety margin under current SLOs, with a tunable lambda to trade throughput vs tail latency.
- Probe budget: default 0.3% of requests; adjustable via per-customer policy.
- Cold start detection: if trace includes >20% prefill tokens, weight prefill probe results more heavily.

Engineering plan:
1) Microprobe harness (C++) + microbench suite (prefill/decode kernels) — 2w
2) Feature pipeline and cheap regressor inference in runtime hot path — 2w
3) Safety layers + policy knobs in config + telemetry exports — 1w
4) Internal canary + dashboarding + A/B results capture — 2w
5) Iteration and stabilization — 2w (approx 9w end-to-end, but MVP for internal canary targeted in 4 weeks).
comments: 2025-02-12 - Michael Liu: Created ticket to capture the funnel scheduler idea after postmortem on prefills for tenant-42. Initial scope focuses on arch + seq-len aware picks and prefill/decode separation.

2025-02-15 - Priya Kapoor: Spike results attached — microprobe harness prototype can execute a candidate kernel micro-benchmark in ~120us on H100 and ~140us on A100 (single-shot, no batching). Estimate probe overhead ~0.15% with current request mix. Suggest increasing probe sample for customers with high variance.

2025-02-19 - Priya Kapoor: Ran offline replay for 24h production trace (mixed chat + completion) with 6 candidate kernels per model. Key findings: for seq-len 32 throughput kernels win on A100, but for seq-len 256 an occupancy-optimized kernel reduces 95p by 42% on H100. Attached perf CSV to PR.

2025-02-22 - Engineering review (Alex Rivera): Concern about model complexity in hot path. Action: use extremely compact regression trees compiled to decision code (no dynamic heap allocation). Also add a runtime switch to disable regressor and fall back to heuristic ordering.

2025-02-25 - Design feedback (Dana Ortiz): Console UX needs a simple explainer for why funnel switched kernels. Proposed a per-request annotation in trace detail + aggregated heatmap of kernel picks by seq-len and arch.

2025-02-27 - QA (Ibrahim Khan): Stress test results attached. Under sustained burst traffic the funnel's probe budget must be rate-limited per-GPU to avoid microprobe contention. Added a rate limiter per compute node in the design.

2025-03-01 - Priya Kapoor: MVP branch opened (runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2783). Microprobe harness code lives under runtime/microprobe. Initial dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-inference/internal/d/kernel-funnel (internal). Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Funnel+Scheduler+Spec.
